This document describes the data pipeline used in this DATA201 project: the inputs, the outputs, the main steps (by week), and the coding strategies we adopted. Cleaning decisions and column definitions are recorded in `README.md` and in the weekly lab notebooks; this file is the pipeline design write-up, not a second data dictionary.

# (1) Inputs

| Input | Source | Role in the pipeline |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Nine monthly Airbnb listing CSVs in `data/` (October 2025–June 2026) | [Inside Airbnb](https://insideairbnb.com/get-the-data/), New Zealand extract, CC BY 4.0 | Raw short-term listing snapshots. Later filtered to Christchurch City only. |
| `data/Detailed-Quarterly-Tenancy-Q1-2020-Q3-2026.csv` | [Tenancy Services](https://www.tenancy.govt.nz/about-tenancy-services/data-and-statistics/rental-bond-data/) | Raw long-term private rental bond statistics (SA2-2019 areas, quarterly). |
| Stats NZ Statistical Area 2 2026 boundaries (Koordinates layer 123515; table 123518) | [datafinder.stats.govt.nz](https://datafinder.stats.govt.nz/table/123518-geographic-areas-table-2026/) via the Koordinates vector query API | Turns Airbnb latitude/longitude into an SA2 `area_code` so listings can be joined to tenancy rows. A local copy of `data/geographic-areas-table-2026.csv` is also in the repo as a reference table. |

Airbnb files were renamed after download so monthly snapshots are identifiable (see `README.md`). The tenancy file is used as published, then filtered in code.

# (2) Outputs

**Intermediate datasets**

- `out/all_chch_listings.csv` — nine months of Christchurch-only Airbnb listings with a `month_year` tag.
- `out/airbnb_cleaned_week_8.csv` — Airbnb file after Week 8 cleaning.
- `out/tenancy_cleaned_week_8.csv` — tenancy file after Week 8 cleaning (Airbnb date window; unusable location ids removed).
- `out/airbnb_with_area_codes.csv` — cleaned Airbnb plus SA2 `area_code` and `area_name` from geocoding.

**Analysis dataset**

- `out/airbnb_tenancy_joined.csv` — left-joined Airbnb listings and area-level tenancy totals by SA2 and quarter.

**Reports**

- `src/week_5_lab_tasks.Rmd`, `src/week_8_lab_airbnb.Rmd`, `src/week_8_lab_tenancy.Rmd`, `src/week_9_lab_tasks.Rmd` — literate notebooks with plots, cleaning notes, and the three Week 9 answers (median price in Christchurch Central; largest short- vs long-term price gap; Airbnb listing counts vs rental bonds by area).

# (3) Main steps

The pipeline keeps raw files untouched and writes a new CSV at each stage. Week 5 builds a Christchurch Airbnb panel. Week 8 cleans that panel and the tenancy bond table independently. Week 9 attaches SA2 codes, joins the two sources, and answers three questions.

```         
```

## Week 5 — combine Christchurch Airbnb snapshots

Notebook: `week_5_lab_tasks.Rmd`.

- Load a monthly file (`june_2026_listings.csv`) and inspect the first rows, `summary()`, and `unique(neighbourhood_group)`.
- Write `load_chch_listings()`: read a monthly CSV, keep `neighbourhood_group == "Christchurch City"`, and add a `month_year` column.
- Apply that function to all nine months (October 2025–June 2026) and `bind_rows()` them into `all_chch`.
- Run exploratory checks: numeric summaries, frequency tables for `room_type` and `neighbourhood`, and missing-value counts.
- Write `data/all_chch_listings.csv`.
- Plot the price distribution (including outliers), calculate days since last review, and inspect the top 10% of listings by number of reviews.

## Week 8 — clean Airbnb

Notebook: `week_8_lab_airbnb.Rmd`.

- Read `data/all_chch_listings.csv` and inspect with `summary()`, `glimpse()`, missingness, and a price histogram.
- Add `scrape_date` from each snapshot’s actual scrape day and compute `days_since_review`.
- Impute missing prices for December 2025–February 2026 only when a listing’s price is the same in every other month it appears.
- Drop listings with price of \$5,000 or more (treated as errors); leave remaining price NAs as NA.
- Drop `license` (entirely missing), `neighbourhood_group` (only Christchurch City), and `host_name` (personally identifiable and unused).
- Recode `reviews_per_month` NA to 0 where there is no last review. Confirm that repeated listing IDs are monthly time-series records, not accidental duplicates.
- Write `out/airbnb_cleaned_week_8.csv`.

## Week 8 — clean tenancy

Notebook: `week_8_lab_tenancy.Rmd`.

- Read the quarterly tenancy CSV and profile structure, including the difference between the text `"NULL"` and true missing values.
- Convert rent columns to numeric (so `"NULL"` becomes NA). Leave `Number Of Beds` as categorical because it includes `ALL` and `5+`.
- Filter `TimeFrame` to 1 October 2025–30 June 2026 so it matches the Airbnb window.
- Replace `"NULL"` in `Location Id` with NA and drop those rows (privacy suppression when counts are too small; the IDs cannot be recovered).
- Drop `Location Id == "-99"` (national totals that inflate means).
- Check for duplicates and for extreme rents; keep the high rents as plausible (large dwellings, low counts).
- Write `out/tenancy_cleaned_week_8.csv`.

## Week 9 — geocode, join, and analyse

Notebook: `week_9_lab_tasks.Rmd`.

- Set up Python through `reticulate`. `query_layer()` and `get_area_info()` call the Koordinates SA2 2026 layer (123515).
- `run_batch_geocoding()` queries unique latitude/longitude pairs only, writes `out/airbnb_with_area_codes.csv`, and skips coordinates that already have an area code.
- Convert Airbnb `month_year` to calendar quarter. Keep tenancy rows where `Dwelling Type == "ALL"` and `Number Of Beds == "ALL"` so there is one tenancy row per area and quarter.
- Left-join on `area_code` and quarter (Airbnb listings are kept even without a tenancy match). Write `out/airbnb_tenancy_joined.csv`.
- Question 1 (Alice): median Airbnb price in Christchurch Central (`area_code` 326600).
- Question 2 (Alisha): nightly price gap (Airbnb price minus median long-term rent / 7), summarised by SA2 and by ward.
- Question 3 (Charlie): unique Airbnb listing counts compared with rental bond counts by area.

# (4) Coding and software strategies

These are practices we used in the repo, including DATA201 lecture themes of reproducible, tidy, documented wrangling.

**Reproducible project layout.** Work lives in an RStudio project (`DATA201.Rproj`). Paths are relative to the project root (`data/...`, `out/...`, `src/...`), not `setwd()`. Package versions are recorded with `renv` (`renv.lock`) so another machine can restore the same R library.

**Do not edit raw data.** Monthly Airbnb files and the original tenancy CSV stay as downloaded (apart from Airbnb filename changes noted in the README). Filtering, imputation, and column drops happen in R Markdown. Each stage writes a new file rather than overwriting the raw input.

**Tidyverse workflow.** Tabular work uses `readr`, `dplyr` pipes, and tibbles. Python is used only for the Koordinates HTTP client, loaded from R with `reticulate`, then results are brought back into R for the join and analysis.

**Literate programming.** Each week is an R Markdown notebook so the code, the reason for a cleaning choice, and the output sit in one place. That matches the course emphasis on documenting wrangling decisions, not only the final table.

**Reducing high cost repeatable steps.** Geocoding is slow and uses an external API. `run_batch_geocoding()` loads `airbnb_with_area_codes.csv` if it exists and only queries coordinates that still lack an `area_code`, so re-knitting does not repeat completed work.

**Version control and collaboration.** The project is a shared GitHub repository. The joined file `airbnb_tenancy_joined.csv` is treated as a shared product: later analysis should not `write_csv()` back to that same name.

**Ethics and data management.** `host_name` was dropped as personally identifiable information that the analysis does not need. Sources, licence (CC BY 4.0 for Inside Airbnb), scrape dates, and limitations are recorded in the README datasheet, in line with course discussion of ethical reuse and attribution.

**Sensitive credentials handling.** API keys are stored in a local, git-ignored `.Renviron` file and read via `os.environ`/`Sys.getenv`, rather than hardcoded in notebooks, so credentials are never committed to version control.

# AI usage

The group used AI on this project, primarily for debugging, code review, and summarising code. Analytical decisions (what to filter, how to impute, how to join, and how to answer the Week 9 questions) were made by the team. AI was used to help implement those decisions, not to choose them.

Tools used: Gemini, Claude, and Cursor (Grok). Cursor (Grok) was used to draft this design-principles document from the existing notebooks and README.
